When I first got ARK: Survival Ascended, I was genuinely satisfied. Yes, I do have a 'good enough' system that handles the game well, so the fact that it's an unoptimized game didn't affect me much at first, and I was fully prepared to drop a positive review. But in only 3 days, my opinion took a complete 180.

I am absolutely pissed over the fact that this version falls into the exact same problem I faced with the old version... storage space. I hate that! I am a casual gamer, I like to play whatever game I am in the mood for at any time. Because of that, I usually keep several games installed on my PC for an easy start and play. But with ASA installed, I have to really pick and choose what else gets to stay on my drive. The fact that this game eats up all your SSD storage is crazy. We are talking about hundreds of gigabytes for a single game, and it only gets worse.

And yeah, sure... I could just add more storage. But have you seen the price of SSDs on the market right now? Convert those prices to my currency (R$) and it is completely insane. I shouldn't have to break the bank just to host one game.

The devs seriously need to clean up the damn game files and stop adding DLC content to the base game. I don't own any of the DLCs, yet I constantly have to keep freeing up space for every single update this game pushes out. There is so much unoptimized junk being forced onto my drive that in just 3 days, the file size increased by almost 60GB. What makes it even worse is how the updates work. Even for a tiny patch, the game demands a massive amount of free space just to unpack and repack its bloated files. I end up having to uninstall other things or completely reinstall the game just to get a minor update to go through.

Because of this massive bloat, my loading times have noticeably increased. Worse yet, the stuttering, which I didn't experience at all when I first installed it, has started to become a huge part of the game. It feels like there is zero optimization…

It only took almost 210gb just the main game and an extra 30gb before I could even get to the main menu and that is just the main game no DLC included whatsoever. Its been 3 years since released, surely they have optimise it by now... Wrong! But fine image looks gorgeous just unplayable, let me play around with the settings surely I will find a better way to get more FPS, turns out the texture popping is because the game doesn't know how to utilize your hardware even if you have a hardware strong enough to run the game, you have to type a command for it to load all textures so the issue stops.... on a 3 years old game. So I lower the settings and managed to get 90fps without any frame gen but the beauty of the game faded, so what is the point?

I get that the game does not want to hold your hand, however, some commands and controls are not obvious and I've had to google, for example, how to drop my pet after picking it up, these things could be explained better.
All that would not have been too bad, but I've had 2 crashes in the last hour, which does not bode too well.My rig is not high-end, but well within the system requirements. It's been in EA since 2023, so I'd expect those kinds of bumps to have been ironed out long ago, so this is disappointing.

Another thing that's crazy is disk space, 200 gig even outstrips my largest game to date. And apparently there are MORE maps to download (for a price, and I'm not sure how I feel about that) if you want to enjoy all of it. Hard to tell after such a short play time how extensive the "base" content maps are.

I'm not (yet) interested in online play, so all I've done has been single player.

I have NEVER IN MY LIFE refunded a game within 5 hours of playing. 

Let's start off:

- It took 10 hours to download. Normally, this is okay. But when you download something for 10 hours and it is THIS BAD.. it means a LOT. 

- Upon entering a server, you will be stuck in place for anywhere from 1-5 entire minutes. 

- Not only are you stuck in place, but you will always load in with a flat 5fps. It will take anywhere from 30 seconds to 2 minutes for the game to load to where you are back at 60fps. You will not be able to do anything during this time. 

- For some reason, lighting is EXTREMELY OFF all the time. Look one way, and everything is a blue foggy mist. Look another way and it's like being upon the gates of hell, red as hell. Don't even get me started on how it looks on the characters too. If you chose pale skin, congrats you're still tan. Doesn't matter. What is the point in customization if I come out a different color (skin, hair, eyebrows) anyway??

- The map. For some really odd reason- waypoint toggling on/off is "off" by default.. I spent an unfortunate amount of time wondering why my waypoints would not highlight in the world. Why the hell is it off by default? Literally WHO benefits from that?? 

- I have a mid PC. I run bulky games like Monster Hunter World w/high res pack and Red Dead Redemption 2 smoothly and beautifully at a capped 60 fps (I could go higher.) The sheer amount of optimization, both in console and in game settings is DIABOLICAL. There is NO excuse for this. Why even release a game like this? 

- Basic HUD/inventory is also extremely laggy.. and for no reason. "Oops I invested 100% of my points into weight because it wouldn't load when I clicked it!!!!" 

- The server I joined was celebrating that they didn't have any crashes in an hour. (This may be unrelated to the game itself, I acknowledge this) like.. Excuse me? We are celebrating a server not crashing.. w…

I want to play this game so bad, but I literally CANNOT get above 20FPS, even on the MAIN MENU. I have plenty of demanding games and they run just fine. This is the only one doing this. So I know it's the unoptimization.

Please, please fix that and I'll come back.

I mean, having to pay for extra dinos that are OP? And maps that add "skill trees?" I don't know what the devs are thinking but they are really out of touch with their audience from ASE. The one thing I really liked is that they added split screen, but the bugs and performance that result during split screen are terrible. And this just having upgraded. I could upgrade- again, but I really don't care to. Most of us aren't going to either.
ASE isn't as pretty but at least it runs well in comparison and doesn't have all these bugs, some of which are the exact same from the original game. Which goes to show they really just wanted to cash grab. I also really don't like the "early access" tags anymore because devs on steam just abuse the hell out of it, including studio wildcard.

ARK: Survival Ascended is one of the most visually impressive survival games available today. Built on Unreal Engine 5, the world looks absolutely stunning, with breathtaking lighting, realistic water, dense forests, and beautifully redesigned dinosaurs. Exploring the map feels more immersive than ever, and the visual upgrade alone makes the game feel like a true next-generation experience.

The gameplay remains as addictive as ever. Taming dinosaurs, building massive bases, exploring dangerous caves, and surviving against both creatures and other players still delivers the unique experience that made ARK so popular. Whether you're playing solo or with friends, there's always something to work toward.

Unfortunately, the game's biggest weakness is its performance. The amount of lag, stuttering, frame drops, and server instability is simply unacceptable. Even on powerful PCs and current-generation consoles, performance can be inconsistent. Large bases, crowded servers, or even normal exploration can cause severe FPS drops and lag spikes that disrupt gameplay. In PvP, these issues can be the difference between winning and losing, making the experience frustrating instead of enjoyable.

Optimization feels unfinished. While the graphics are incredible, the game often struggles to run smoothly enough to let players fully appreciate them. It's disappointing because the technical issues constantly get in the way of an otherwise amazing survival experience.

Despite these problems, ARK: Survival Ascended has incredible potential. The core gameplay is still one of the best in the survival genre, and the graphical overhaul is outstanding. If the developers continue improving optimization, reducing lag, and making servers more stable, this could easily become the definitive version of ARK.

citations.review_text: This is a bizarre continuation to the original game. I really enjoy the improvements in graphics, sometimes the game is breathtaking in the way it looks. Even so it is insanely unoptimized, I have a Ryzen 7 7800x3d and an RX 7900XT and somehow I'm struggling to get 60fps on medium settings (1440p native )... Furthermore the creature design has suffered a lot, many of the new tames don't feel like they belong in a map's ecosystem like the original ones did, some stand out so much that they feel completely out of place on any map. Plus many of those new creatures require a DLC to interact with or to tame, despite already spawning in the world - which feels disrespectful. On top of that the release was premature and even years after it still has a lot less content than its Evolved counterpart. I am glad that I did not pay the full price for this game as it is bloated and unfinished, and it's frustrating because I genuinely enjoy ARK and want a good successor for it.

I love this game. Despite that, I wouldn’t recommend it. This game is a sham and a cash grab. None of the promises have been kept. I haven’t written a review before, but enough is enough.

If you want to buy all the DLC, it’ll set you back €195!!! Plus, almost all of these DLCs are just cash grabs that add nothing of value.

Bob’s Tall Tales (€30): One of the few worth getting, but still—€30 for 3 vehicles and three dinos.

Lost Colony (€30): The DLC that adds a map, 2 dinos, a pay-to-win skill tree, a boss that feels more like *Elden Ring* than *ARK*, and vampires. The map is completely different from all the others—and not in a good way. They could have made it one of the best maps in the game; instead, it’s supposed to be set in an ultra-advanced research lab, yet we end up with a medieval theme and vampires. I know the devs love that whole universe, but honestly, just make a separate map outside the main story. Plus, at launch—and even now—the game runs terribly on this map; I get at least 20 to 40 fewer FPS here.

ARK Astraeos (€15): The only good new map, and it wasn’t even made by the actual game developers—it was made by a f***ing modder.

Tribe of Fortune (€20): An unfinished DLC! On an unfinished map! It adds boats that duel with dinos and some skins; it’s shameful to release a DLC in this state. It’s empty and just an unfinished cash grab. Plus, pirates in *ARK Genesis*—which is supposed to be an ultra-futuristic simulation with teleportation...

Dragontopia (€30): Shameful; nothing else to say. €30 for two dragons, a set of armor, and a tool. €30!!! There are mods that offer way more content. This whole thing is a total rip-off—a cash grab by Snail Games for their electric car brand...

"Fantastic" tames—€30 for dinos? No, these are fantasy creatures that would fit better in the world of Harry Potter than in ARK. Plus, this crap is pay-to-win; I'm really disappointed.

€30+€30+€20+€15+€30+€30 = €155 in DLC—it’s like something out of Ubisoft or EA. On top…

It was incredibly difficult for me to write this review because I truly love
this game. ARK has been a huge part of my life for years, but I can no longer
ignore the direction it’s taking. I feel forced to write this because the
current state of things is simply unacceptable.

I am writing this with over 8,000 hours of experience in ARK on Playstation and
a significant amount of time here on Steam. I know this game inside and
out—every mechanic and every flaw. What Wildcard is delivering here with ARK:
Survival Ascended (ASA) is nothing short of a tragedy.

The Lie About Price & Monetization: Originally, Co-Founder Jeremy Stieglitz
promised that ASA would be a free upgrade for owners of ASE. The reality? It has
become one of the most heavily monetized games out there. Being forced to pay
double and triple for a "remake" that was promised for free is absolutely
brazen.

Broken Promises as a Tradition: There is one thing you can always count on: the
developers never keep their word regarding release dates. Delays aren't the
exception; they’ve become a tradition. This clearly shows that the studio
refuses to learn from its mistakes—or worse, they simply don't care about their
players' time.

Pay-to-Win (P2W) Destroying the Meta: We have reached the point of €5 tames (and
the price trend is rising). The Pyromane is the perfect example: it is so
incredibly overpowered that you are forced to buy it just to keep up with the
meta. This makes fighting extremely dull and repetitive because everyone just
"pops" that one specific paid tame.

Bugs, Exploits, and Technical Failure: While the patch notes list occasional
fixes, the game remains infested with bugs, exploits, and hackers. Instead of
stabilizing the game, they prioritize working on new paid content to milk the
players. The absolute peak of this was the Genesis Hexagon Exploit: it was
proven that the code was copied 1:1 from the old ASE. When ASA launched, they
likely accidentally left it in, which led to massive rollb…

They spend more time optimizing their DLC trailers so it looks like a well developed game that runs smooth. In reality, it is a glitching, stuttering, lagging, desyncing, rubber banding piece of trash they want you to pay a premium for.

Ark is the original example of an early access game. Survival Evolved entered early access over ten years ago and never really left it. Survival Ascended is more a remaster than a sequel. Ark is the prime example of predatory pricing and early access release policy. Nothing ever works quite right; in order to keep up with other players, you have absolutely no choice but to buy the new DLC -- it is non-negotiable, because every DLC introduces a paradigm-shifting set of items, mechanics, or tameable pets.

The game preys on the sunk cost fallacy by requiring you to put in several dozen hours to make any sort of progress. It dazzles you with the spectacle of its environments and landscapes, which themselves are actually quite pretty, as well as the creatures; not that you'll be able to actually appreciate them on anything but the highest end hardware -- and in many cases, not even then, because their optimizaiton is still a joke as it was 10 years ago.

You can see I have over 100 hours in Survival Ascended; I have over 500 in Survival Evolved. All of those hours are reflective of the lowest points of my life when I threw myself head long into a game that only rewards obsessive play and sunk cost. The game itself isn't actually rewarding. I regretted buying Survival Evolved, and I ignored my better instincts to buy Survival Ascended.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that official servers suffer from a lack of capacity during major releases, resulting in long wait times to join or being disconnected randomly.

citations.review_text:
ARK: Survival Ascended is the ultimate testament to a developer having brilliant ideas but lacking absolutely any of the competence required to execute them. Snail Games and Studio Wildcard have a goldmine of a concept, but they bury it under a mountain of broken promises, technical disasters, and blatant disrespect for their player base.

Every single map release or major patch is a certified trainwreck. Instead of exciting new content, an update in ASA is a gamble on whether your hard work will survive. It is a near-guarantee that updates will break the game entirely, frequently resulting in players completely losing their progression, bases, and maxed characters. Wildcard doesn't just push buggy patches; they push game-destroying ones.

They will gladly take your money for new DLCs, but don't expect them to actually work. Worse yet, even if the DLC manages to run, good luck actually getting to experience it. Wildcard consistently refuses to launch enough servers to accommodate the player base during new content drops. Servers are perpetually capped at maximum capacity, meaning tons of paying customers are left sitting at the menu, unable to play the very content they just paid for.

Perhaps the most infuriating part of dealing with Studio Wildcard is their abysmal communication. When the game inevitably breaks during peak issue times or catastrophic launches, the developers go completely radio silent. It is normal for the community to go days without a single update, acknowledgment, or apology while the game is in a literally unplayable state.

The Bottom Line: Do not reward this developer with your time or money. Until Wildcard learns how to properly test a patch, communicate with their community, and actually provide the server infrastructure people pay for, ARK: Survival Ascended is nothing more than a frustrating exercise in wasted potential.

Let's give them 7 and a half servers for everyone to compete for, and spend 99% of your time playing join simulator. I wish I could get a refund. Yikes.

If you enjoy 2 hours of clicking to get onto official servers to be booted at random around 20 minutes into doing anything. Then buy this game.  1/10th the number of servers needed for a new MAP/DLC release.

I've been playing ARK for over 11 years, and this is nothing new. Every major launch seems to be the same story: a bad launch, little to no communication, and nowhere near enough servers for people to actually play.

If you want to spend 10 hours trying to join a server, only to disconnect 30 minutes later and lose everything, this is the perfect experience.

The community has become incredibly toxic, but that's what happens when players are constantly frustrated by problems that never seem to get fixed. Most of that anger starts with the state of the game and the lack of communication from the developers.

Everyone who paid for this deserves a refund. Honestly, even if it were free, a lot of people still wouldn't play because, right now, it's simply unplayable.
